channel.title: Happy News Company
channel.description: Real, sourced good news and good-news press releases

item.title: A Chemist Who Lived to 103 Leaves $24 Million to Science Students at a New Jersey Community College
item.description: Raritan Valley Community College says the estate of Dr. Carlyle "Corky" Gordon Caldwell has given it the largest private gift in its history, for science scholarships and a future science center.

item.title: Researchers in Spain Use Vitamin B12 as a Catalyst in an Experimental Rechargeable Battery
item.description: The laboratory prototype ran for up to 250 charge cycles, an early step toward batteries made with natural materials.

item.title: FIGS and Noah Wyle Pledge $2 Million to Help Erase at Least $200 Million in Medical Debt
item.description: A three-year partnership with Undue Medical Debt aims to relieve debt for more than 150,000 Americans, with a first round planned before the holidays.

item.title: Olive Ridley Hatchlings Released in Southern California After First Confirmed Sea Turtle Nests on the U.S. West Coast
item.description: Eggs moved ahead of a storm hatched at the Aquarium of the Pacific, and the young turtles crawled to the sea on November 14 and 15.

item.title: Drones Catch Humpback Whale Breath, and Scientists Read Whole Genomes From It
item.description: Researchers sequenced genomes from the exhaled spray of 26 whales off British Columbia without needing to take tissue samples.

item.title: Warren Buffett Gives Away About $5.5 Billion in Berkshire Shares in His Annual Thanksgiving Gift
item.description: The donation to four family foundations is part of a plan to give away all of his Berkshire stock.

item.title: FDA Approves Klygefa, a Once-Weekly Self-Injected Treatment for Generalized Myasthenia Gravis
item.description: The nanobody drug from Alexion and AstraZeneca is approved for adults with the most common form of the muscle-weakness disease.

item.title: Eritrea Becomes the 34th Country to Eliminate Trachoma as a Public Health Problem
item.description: The World Health Organization validated the milestone on 16 November after two decades of work against the world's leading infectious cause of blindness.

item.title: Native Oysters Are Breeding in Scotland's Dornoch Firth for the First Time in Over a Century
item.description: Baby oysters found by Heriot-Watt University scientists show a restoration project launched in 2017 is starting to pay off.

item.title: Lake Baikal's Water Supply Is Recovering After Decades of Decline, Tree-Ring Study Finds
item.description: Streamflow into the world's most voluminous freshwater lake has run well above average since 2017, though researchers say it is early days.

item.title: FDA Approves the First Drug Made for Primary Membranous Nephropathy, a Rare Kidney Disease
item.description: A phase 3 trial found far more adults reached complete remission of protein leakage with Gazyva than with tacrolimus.

item.title: "Forever Chemicals" Fall in England's Rivers and Fish, Environment Agency Report Finds
item.description: Levels of PFOS and PFOA in English rivers dropped by about 30% between 2016 and 2025, and PFOS in freshwater fish fell by roughly 49%.

item.title: Two Remote Pacific Atolls, Now a Marine Sanctuary, Are Called Among Earth's Best Reference Ecosystems
item.description: A new survey of Bikar and Bokak in the Marshall Islands found thriving seabird colonies, turtle nests and reef fish, plus 14 groups never before recorded in the country.

item.title: Europe's Hera Spacecraft Reaches the Asteroid NASA Nudged and Sends Back Its First Close-Up
item.description: After a two-year journey, Hera is beginning a "crash site investigation" of the first test of planetary defense.

item.title: Ethiopian Water Mouse, Known From One Animal Collected in 1927, Is Found Again
item.description: A survey team in the Yayu Biosphere Reserve caught a rodent feared lost for nearly a century.

item.title: Doctors Report First Transplant of Organ-Donor Bone Marrow for a Non-Cancerous Blood Disease
item.description: A 40-year-old woman with severe aplastic anemia no longer needs transfusions six months after a transplant using marrow from a deceased organ donor.

item.title: FDA Approves Pimjetmi, a Once-Daily Pill for a Rare Joint Tumor
item.description: The approval gives adults with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor a new oral option when surgery could cause lasting harm.

item.title: Kansas Group That Welcomed Algeria's World Cup Team Gets a Hero's Welcome in Algeria
item.description: Thirty-eight people from Lawrence, Kansas, including students and police officers, were invited to Algeria after their World Cup hospitality went viral.

item.title: FDA Approves Bayer's Sunharbo, the First Factor XIa Inhibitor, to Help Prevent a Second Stroke
item.description: A once-daily pill taken with antiplatelet therapy cut ischemic stroke risk by 26% in a 12,327-person trial.

item.title: Ten Years After a Scallop-Dredging Ban, Scotland's Summer Isles Are Brimming With Life
item.description: Protected maerl beds are now breeding grounds for herring, cod and haddock, thanks to a campaign by divers, fishermen and locals.

item.title: Oracle Gives $1.55 Million to Turn a Nashville Church Property Into a Community Hub
item.description: The grant will fund a new dining room and free events at Trinity Community Commons, part of a larger East Nashville project that includes 22 affordable homes.

item.title: Airbnb's Brian Chesky Pledges $100 Million to San Francisco Parks, the City's Largest Single-Donor Gift
item.description: The money will speed up new parks, keep pools open longer and help finish waterfront projects, starting with five sites.

item.title: A Garden-Shed Breeding Project Is Bringing Glowworms Back to a Yorkshire Nature Reserve
item.description: Volunteer Peter Cooper has reared about 1,900 larvae for release at Nosterfield, where the insects haven't been seen in roughly a century.

item.title: U.S. Homelessness Fell an Estimated 6.7% in 2026, the Biggest Yearly Drop Since 2007
item.description: An independent analysis of national count data suggests about 49,000 fewer people were homeless on a single night, with veteran homelessness down nearly 8%.

item.title: China's CO2 Emissions Fell 3.1% in Q3, With Electric Cars at a Record 67% of Sales
item.description: A Carbon Brief analysis finds the biggest quarterly drop since the 2022 Covid lockdowns, driven by clean power and EVs.

item.title: China Connects a 600 MWh Liquid-Air Battery to Its Grid in Qinghai
item.description: The Golmud plant turns surplus renewable power into liquid air, then back into electricity for up to 10 hours.

item.title: Species Down to Fewer Than 50 Animals Often Bounce Back When People Step In, Study Finds
item.description: A review of every bird and mammal that fell below 50 wild individuals since 1950 found that most helped by direct conservation action recovered to at least 100.

item.title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to First New Head and Neck Cancer Option in a Decade
item.description: Rybrevant Faspro shrank tumors in 42% of patients in a 102-person trial, though the approval is conditional on confirmatory studies.

item.title: New Jersey Warehouse Roofs Will Host 16 Community Solar Projects, Half Reserved for Lower-Income Households
item.description: Industrial property owner Faropoint plans more than 10 MW of rooftop solar that adds clean power without using any new land.

item.title: 280 Ice Age Engravings Found Hiding in Plain Sight in a Catalan Cave
item.description: Visitors have toured Cova de la Font Major for decades, scratching their own names over art made by Palaeolithic people.

item.title: Antarctic Blue Whales Have Rebounded to About 4,000 Animals, New Study Estimates
item.description: Researchers combined whaling records and modern surveys to show the world's largest animal growing about 4.5% a year, though it is still far below its historic numbers.

item.title: WHO: 63 Countries Have Eliminated a Neglected Tropical Disease, and Guinea Worm Hits a Record Low
item.description: A mid-term review finds real gains since 2020, along with a warning that funding is the biggest threat to 2030 goals.

item.title: Puzzling Gas Over Mars Volcano Hints the Red Planet May Not Be Geologically Dead
item.description: Europe's ExoMars orbiter keeps spotting hydrogen chloride above fresh cracks on Alba Mons, and scientists say it could point to a dormant magma system.

item.title: Pet Dogs Can Be Trained to Sniff Out Invasive Plants, German Study Finds
item.description: In a feasibility trial, volunteer owners and their dogs learned to detect species like Himalayan balsam with 75% average success.

item.title: 110,000 Documents on Saving Venice After the 1966 Flood to Be Digitised
item.description: On the flood's 60th anniversary, UNESCO and the Fondazione Giorgio Cini begin a two-year project to open the archive to everyone.

item.title: Newborn Deaths in Flint Halved After Cash Payments to Expecting Families, Study Finds
item.description: Michigan State researchers link the Rx Kids program to a drop in neonatal mortality, though the study is early and observational.

item.title: First Generic Version of Twice-Yearly HIV Prevention Shot Clears FDA Review
item.description: Dr. Reddy's lenacapavir, aimed at 120 lower-income countries, is expected to cost about $40 a person per year.

item.title: North Atlantic Right Whales Had 23 Calves in 2026, the Most Since 2009
item.description: NOAA data show shorter gaps between births for returning mothers, and a Florida festival this weekend celebrates the whales' return, though the species remains endangered.

item.title: Venomous Primate Feared Extinct for Nearly a Century Is Still Alive in Indonesia
item.description: A new study says the Bangka slow loris survives on Bangka Island, with rescue records pointing to a wider range than thought.

item.title: A Dubai Infant Who Had 110 Seizures a Day Is Seizure-Free After an Experimental Drug
item.description: Doctors at King's College Hospital London – Dubai report the baby's seizures stopped within 30 minutes of a first dose, though the medicine is still in clinical trials.
